lines.text: Everyone knows the love story of Sanyogita and Prithviraj Chauhan.
But how much of it really happened?
This is the historical truth about Rani Sanyogita.
Kannauj, on the Ganga. Princess Sanyogita, daughter of Raja Jaichand, grows up hearing songs of a fearless young king.
He is Prithviraj Chauhan of Ajmer. She has never met him — she has only seen his portrait.
The legend says she lost her heart to him, and he to her.
Jaichand announces a swayamvara: his daughter will choose her own husband.
Every king is invited except his rival, Prithviraj. To mock him, Jaichand puts his statue at the door, as a doorkeeper.
Sanyogita walks past every waiting king…
…and places her garland around the statue's neck.
Prithviraj, hidden nearby, steps out and lifts her onto his horse…
…and they ride away into the night.
It's one of India's best-loved romances.
But the legend ends in tragedy: Jaichand's fury, a divided north, and Prithviraj's fall to Muhammad of Ghor at Tarain, in 1192.
lines.say: But the legend ends in tragedy: Jaichand's fury, a divided north, and Prithviraj's fall to Muhammad of Ghor at Tarain, in eleven ninety-two.

lines.text: So what does history actually say? Let's look at the evidence.
The whole story comes from one source: the Prithviraj Raso, an epic poem credited to Chand Bardai, Prithviraj's court poet.
But its surviving versions were written down centuries later, full of added verses. Historians read it as poetry, not a record.
A poem from Prithviraj's own lifetime does exist: the Sanskrit Prithviraja Vijaya, by his court poet Jayanaka.
It praises his family, his court and his battles — but in the part that survives, Sanyogita never appears.
Jaichand's own copper-plate grants name his son and heir, Harishchandra — but never a daughter.
Then again, grants like these rarely named daughters at all.
Later tellings don't even agree on her name — Sanyogita, Sanjogita, Samyukta — or on what became of her.
What is real is the rivalry: Jaichand of the Gahadavala dynasty ruled Kannauj and Varanasi, while Prithviraj ruled from Ajmer to Delhi.
And no source of the time says Jaichand betrayed him. He fell to the same invader at Chandawar, in 1194.
lines.say: And no source of the time says Jaichand betrayed him. He fell to the same invader at Chandawar, in eleven ninety-four.

lines.text: So, was Sanyogita real? Many historians see the romance as a poet's invention.
Others think a real princess and a real elopement may lie behind it — remembered, and embellished, by the bards.
Sanyogita lives in poetry, not in stone.
But for eight hundred years, people have kept her story alive — and that is part of history too.
